From: Asha Menon <finance@acmecloud.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2028 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Unusual hourly billing duplicates - need reconciliation

Hi Vivek —

We're seeing a set of duplicated hourly meter slices on our AWS Marketplace invoices for April 16 that are pushing up both the gross usage and the VAT posted to our EU entity. Attached is a small extract (acme_hourly_slices_0416.csv) showing repeated slice_ids for the same resource across two adjacent hours (00:00-01:00 UTC and 01:00-02:00 UTC). The seller SKU is redwood-inference-prod and the meter_id appears twice with different seller-side timestamps.

High-level impact: exploratory totals show ~12.8k USD in duplicated charges and VAT was applied to the wrong legal entity for ~40% of the duplicated lines (we're in the EU nexus).

Can your team confirm whether Redwood emitted duplicate slice_ids or if our ingestion matched the same slice twice? We need a reconciliation plan and a proposed credit memo so we can temporarily hold the payment for the disputed amount while we sort this out.

Attachments: acme_hourly_slices_0416.csv (CSV — 84 rows)

Thanks,
Asha Menon
Head of Finance — Acme Cloud

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2028 13:48:05 -0700
Subject: internal: RE: Unusual hourly billing duplicates - need reconciliation

Vivek / Monica —

I've pulled metering logs for the affected window. Quick technical summary: during a midnight migration of the hourly aggregator (we rolled a small change at 00:58 UTC), there was a short window where the aggregation worker restarted and re-emitted a batch of hourly slices without marking them as acknowledged. That produced duplicate slice_ids for approximately 3.2k unique meters where the upstream idempotency key was transiently unset.

Evidence: I've attached a trimmed log with the collision pattern (metering_collision_snippet.log). The duplicated slices have identical slice_id but different "emitted_at" timestamps separated by about 62 seconds. The ingestion pipeline on the Marketplace side accepted both records and mapped them to separate invoice lines.

Mitigation & next steps (technical):
- Patch aggregator to persist acknowledgement before re-emitting (deployed in canary at 14:10 PT).
- Backfill a dedupe pass to mark the later-emitted duplicates and flag them for seller reporting (ETA: 24 hours).
- Export a per-slice checksum bundle (JSON lines) for matching with the seller report — I'll drop that into our shared GDrive folder when ready.

Estimate of duplicated USD exposure: ~$12,842.50 (gross usage only). VAT reallocation will be handled by Finance but note we should include seller invoice ids to avoid double-crediting.

-Karthik
Senior Engineer, Metering — Redwood Inference

Attachment: metering_collision_snippet.log (plain text — excerpt)
From: Asha Menon <finance@acmecloud.com>

Vivek —

Thanks for the quick responses and the internal note, Karthik. I've attached the full AWS seller export for April 16 (aws_seller_report_0416.xlsx) — it includes the invoice ids and VAT allocation columns.

We prefer per-invoice credits so our AR ledger can match the refunds to invoice lines. On VAT: please propose VAT reallocation entries per invoice; if Redwood can provide corrected invoice lines with the proper EU entity tax tags, we can apply credit memos and re-post VAT on our side.

Two small asks: 1) can you provide an initial estimate of the credit amount within 24 hours so we can flag the dispute in our ERP, and 2) please confirm whether Redwood will issue a single consolidated credit memo or multiple smaller credit memos aligned to the Marketplace invoice ids.

Attachments: aws_seller_report_0416.xlsx (Excel — 1.2 MB)

Best,
Asha
